site.name: codekite
site.summary: codekite-clone Fictional cloud CI/CD service "CodeKite CI" marketing site, focused on the pricing-page usage calculator. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Short landing: hero (YAML code example on the right), 3 feature cards, CTA to pricing | | `pricing.html` | Main page: 3 plan cards (Free / Team / Enterprise) + usage calculator (three slider+number pairs linked two-way: build minutes / concurrency / storage + ARM / macOS / GPU runner checkboxes); right-side sticky monthly total + recommended-plan badge + line-item cost breakdown; below: 16-row plan comparison table; 10-question FAQ accordion; trusted-logo row; 4-column footer | | `docs.html` | Placeholder quickstart page (one YAML example) |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full codekite system, prioritizing the primary pricing flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The exploration achieved high coverage across both desktop and mobile viewports, heavily exercising the interactive pricing calculator. While the calculator's real-time cost breakdown performs excellently and provides clear feedback, several critical accessibility and mobile usability issues were identified. Form inputs lack programmatic labels for screen readers, and touch targets for checkboxes and navigation links are significantly undersized for mobile users.

exploration_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the CodeKite marketing site, with a deep focus on the pricing page's interactive usage calculator and plan comparisons.
exploration_plan.summary: The run will begin by validating the landing page layout and top-level navigation. It will then dedicate significant effort to the pricing page, rigorously testing the two-way bound usage calculator (sliders vs. number inputs) and the dynamic cost breakdown. The run will also review the docs placeholder and conclude with a mobile viewport pass to evaluate responsive scaling and tap target issues flagged in the prescan.
assumptions: The pricing calculator on pricing.html uses JavaScript for real-time calculation and two-way binding between sliders and numeric inputs.
The FAQ section on pricing.html is likely implemented as an interactive accordion.
Docs.html is a placeholder but should still be reachable and well-formatted.
risk_hotspots: pricing.html: Usage calculator two-way binding (slider vs number input).
pricing.html: Real-time calculation accuracy and UI updates (total cost, recommended plan badge, line items).
pricing.html: Missing input labels on calculator controls (accessibility risk).
Global: Small tap targets on navigation links (mobile usability risk).

phases.title: Landing Page & Navigation
phases.objective: Verify the homepage layout, hero section, and top-level navigation.
key_checks: Verify hero CTA buttons lead to the correct pages (Pricing, Docs).
exit_criteria: Navigation links are confirmed to route correctly to pricing.html and docs.html.

phases.title: Pricing Calculator Interaction
phases.objective: Stress-test the interactive usage calculator on the pricing page.
key_checks: Drag sliders for 'Build minutes', 'Concurrent builds', and 'Storage' and verify numeric inputs update.
Type values into numeric inputs and verify sliders snap to corresponding positions.
Toggle runner checkboxes (ARM, macOS, GPU) and verify they affect the calculated total.
Observe the sticky monthly total, line-item breakdown, and 'recommended-plan' badge for accurate updates based on input.
Verify accessibility of the inputs given the 'missing_input_label' prescan warnings.
exit_criteria: Calculator inputs (both slider and typed) have been exercised, and the UI correctly reflects the dynamic cost.

phases.title: Pricing Plans & FAQ
phases.objective: Validate static pricing content and interactive FAQ.
key_checks: Review the 3 main plan cards (Free, Team, Enterprise).
Scroll through the 16-row plan comparison table for readability.
Interact with the 10-question FAQ accordion to ensure it expands/collapses properly.
exit_criteria: Plan cards, comparison table, and FAQ accordion have been viewed and interacted with.

phases.title: Docs Placeholder Validation

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Pass
phases.objective: Evaluate mobile responsiveness and touch usability.
key_checks: Verify if the navigation collapses into a hamburger menu and functions.
Test the pricing calculator sliders on a small screen layout.
Assess the impact of the 'small_tap_target' warnings on mobile usability.
exit_criteria: Core pages have been viewed in mobile mode, and critical interactions (navigation, calculator) have been re-tested.

coverage_targets.features: Exercise all pricing calculator inputs (sliders, typeable fields, checkboxes) and the FAQ accordion.
coverage_targets.mobile: Re-run navigation and pricing calculator checks in a mobile viewport.

notes: The prescan highlights missing input labels on the pricing calculator. This should be explicitly noted in the UX critique as an accessibility failure.
Pay close attention to how the 'sticky monthly total' behaves when scrolling on both desktop and mobile.

findings.user_goal: Understand and interact with the pricing calculator using assistive technologies.
findings.problem: The range sliders and their corresponding numeric input fields lack programmatic labels, `aria-label` attributes, or placeholders.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings flag multiple inputs in the calculator (ux-7 through ux-12, including range and number types) as missing accessible labels.
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users will not receive context for what these sliders and inputs control (e.g., 'Build minutes', 'Concurrent builds'), making the pricing calculator virtually unusable for them.
findings.suggestion: Add explicitly linked `<label>` elements (using `for` and `id` attributes) or descriptive `aria-label` attributes to both the range sliders and their matching numeric input fields.

findings.user_goal: Select add-on runners (e.g., macOS, GPU) on a mobile device to estimate total cost.
findings.problem: The add-on runner checkboxes have a touch target of 13x13px, falling significantly below standard mobile accessibility guidelines (e.g., 44x44px).
findings.evidence: Observation data and layout warnings for mobile viewports flag the checkboxes (ux-13, ux-14, ux-15) as having tap targets of 13x13px.
findings.why_it_matters: Users on mobile devices will struggle to accurately tap these tiny checkboxes, leading to frustration, misclicks, and difficulty in estimating their costs.
findings.suggestion: Increase the interactive area by wrapping the checkbox and its text in a single `<label>` element, and apply CSS padding to ensure the total clickable area is at least 44x44px.

findings.user_goal: Navigate the site easily using the header and footer links on a mobile device.
findings.problem: Header navigation links and footer links have vertical heights that are too small for comfortable touch interaction on mobile devices.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings highlight that header links like 'Pricing' (49x21px) and footer links (~26px high) are below the 44px mobile guidance.
findings.why_it_matters: Tightly packed, small links are difficult to tap accurately on touch screens, increasing the cognitive load and the risk of accidental misclicks for mobile users.
findings.suggestion: Increase the vertical padding on navigation links (both in the global header and the footer grid) to ensure they meet the minimum 44px height requirement for touch targets.
findings.source_hint: Header and footer `<a>` elements across index.html and pricing.html

findings.user_goal: Understand the total expected monthly cost based on selected usage.
findings.problem: Adjusting certain sliders (like Concurrent Builds) upgrades the 'Recommended plan' to a paid tier (e.g., Team or Enterprise), but the 'Estimated Monthly' total does not include the base cost or per-user fees of that recommended plan; it only calculates usage add-ons.
findings.evidence: During steps 43-48, increasing concurrent builds changed the recommended plan to 'Enterprise' due to workload caps, but the estimated monthly dollar total remained unchanged since no usage add-ons were selected.
findings.why_it_matters: Users might mistakenly believe the 'Estimated Monthly' total represents their entire bill, leading to a false expectation and subsequent trust issues if base plan fees (like the $39/user/month for Team) are not factored into the calculator's bottom line.
findings.suggestion: Clarify the pricing breakdown. Either explicitly include the base plan cost in the calculation when a paid plan is recommended, or clearly label the total amount as 'Estimated Usage Cost (Excludes Base Plan Fees)'.
